content:
Consider the following snippet, which is a start at formalising the theory of icosians:

import Mathlib.Analysis.Quaternion
import Mathlib.NumberTheory.Real.GoldenRatio

noncomputable section
open goldenRatio Quaternion

/-- The unit icosian `(1 + i + j + k) / 2`, which has order 6. -/
def icosian6 : ℍˣ where
  val := ⟨2⁻¹, 2⁻¹, 2⁻¹, 2⁻¹⟩
  inv := star ⟨2⁻¹, 2⁻¹, 2⁻¹, 2⁻¹⟩
  val_inv := by rw [self_mul_star ⟨_, _, _, _⟩, normSq_def' ⟨_, _, _, _⟩]; norm_num
  inv_val := by rw [star_mul_self ⟨_, _, _, _⟩, normSq_def' ⟨_, _, _, _⟩]; norm_num

/-- The unit icosian `(φ + i + ψ*j) / 2`, which has order 10. -/
def icosian10 : ℍˣ where
  val := ⟨φ / 2, 2⁻¹, ψ / 2, 0⟩
  inv := star ⟨φ / 2, 2⁻¹, ψ / 2, 0⟩
  val_inv := by rw [self_mul_star ⟨_, _, _, _⟩, ← coe_one, coe_inj, normSq_def' ⟨_, _, _, _⟩]; grind
  inv_val := by rw [star_mul_self ⟨_, _, _, _⟩, ← coe_one, coe_inj, normSq_def' ⟨_, _, _, _⟩]; grind

/-- The unit icosians. -/
def Icosian : Subgroup ℍˣ := Subgroup.closure {icosian6, icosian10}

The ⟨_, _, _, _⟩ are necessary, otherwise I get the following error:

Tactic `rewrite` failed: Did not find an occurrence of the pattern
  ?a * star ?a
in the target expression
  { re := 2⁻¹, imI := 2⁻¹, imJ := 2⁻¹, imK := 2⁻¹ } * star { re := 2⁻¹, imI := 2⁻¹, imJ := 2⁻¹, imK := 2⁻¹ } = 1

⊢ { re := 2⁻¹, imI := 2⁻¹, imJ := 2⁻¹, imK := 2⁻¹ } * star { re := 2⁻¹, imI := 2⁻¹, imJ := 2⁻¹, imK := 2⁻¹ } = 1


Note: The target expression is not type-correct under the `implicit` transparency level, which may have triggered the failure. This is usually caused by unfolding of semireducible definitions in prior tactic steps. Use `set_option linter.tacticCheckInstances true` to investigate the source of the issue.
Full error:
  Application type mismatch: The argument
    { re := 2⁻¹, imI := 2⁻¹, imJ := 2⁻¹, imK := 2⁻¹ }
  has type
    ℍ[ℝ,-1,-1]
  but is expected to have type
    ℍ
  in the application
    HMul.hMul { re := 2⁻¹, imI := 2⁻¹, imJ := 2⁻¹, imK := 2⁻¹ }

Does this error indicate a problem with the definition of quaternions, and if so how can it be fixed?
What's the reason that docs#Quaternion is a def instead of an abbrev?

Even this does not work:

OK, with Quaternion as an abbrev, this does work:

import Mathlib.Algebra.Quaternion
import Mathlib.Data.Real.Basic

open Quaternion QuaternionAlgebra

/-- The unit icosian `(1 + i + j + k) / 2`, which has order 6. -/
noncomputable def icosian6 : ℍ[ℝ]ˣ where
  val := ⟨2⁻¹, 2⁻¹, 2⁻¹, 2⁻¹⟩
  inv := ⟨2⁻¹, -2⁻¹, -2⁻¹, -2⁻¹⟩
  val_inv := by rw [mk_mul_mk]; ext <;> norm_num
  inv_val := by rw [mk_mul_mk]; ext <;> norm_num

Aaron Liu said:

What's the reason that docs#Quaternion is a def instead of an abbrev?

Looking at the blame, Quaternion has been a def ever since Mathlib.Algebra.Quaternion was ported

Jeremy Tan said:

OK, with Quaternion as an abbrev, this does work:

Does tagging Quaternion with instance_reducible work?

Edison Xie said:

Does tagging Quaternion with instance_reducible work?

Yes

I have opened #43078 which makes Quaternion instance-reducible and adds some helper lemmas on the transformation of Quaternion coordinates by the basic operations, which makes the following code work:

import Mathlib.Analysis.Quaternion
import Mathlib.NumberTheory.Real.GoldenRatio

noncomputable section
open goldenRatio Quaternion

/-- The unit icosian `(1 + i + j + k) / 2`, which has order 6. -/
def icosian6 : ℍˣ where
  val := ⟨2⁻¹, 2⁻¹, 2⁻¹, 2⁻¹⟩
  inv := ⟨2⁻¹, -2⁻¹, -2⁻¹, -2⁻¹⟩
  val_inv := by rw [mk_mul_mk, mk_one]; norm_num
  inv_val := by rw [mk_mul_mk, mk_one]; norm_num

/-- The unit icosian `(φ + i + ψ*j) / 2`, which has order 10. -/
def icosian10 : ℍˣ where
  val := ⟨φ / 2, 2⁻¹, ψ / 2, 0⟩
  inv := ⟨φ / 2, -2⁻¹, -ψ / 2, 0⟩
  val_inv := by rw [mk_mul_mk, mk_one]; grind
  inv_val := by rw [mk_mul_mk, mk_one]; grind

/-- The unit icosians. -/
def Icosian : Subgroup ℍˣ := Subgroup.closure {icosian6, icosian10}

Jeremy Tan said:

I have opened #43078 which makes Quaternion instance-reducible

Making it implicit_reducible works too:

import Mathlib.Analysis.Quaternion
import Mathlib.NumberTheory.Real.GoldenRatio

noncomputable section
open goldenRatio Quaternion

attribute [local implicit_reducible] Quaternion

/-- The unit icosian `(1 + i + j + k) / 2`, which has order 6. -/
def icosian6 : ℍˣ where
  val := ⟨2⁻¹, 2⁻¹, 2⁻¹, 2⁻¹⟩
  inv := star ⟨2⁻¹, 2⁻¹, 2⁻¹, 2⁻¹⟩
  val_inv := by rw [self_mul_star, normSq_def']; norm_num
  inv_val := by rw [star_mul_self, normSq_def']; norm_num

/-- The unit icosian `(φ + i + ψ*j) / 2`, which has order 10. -/
def icosian10 : ℍˣ where
  val := ⟨φ / 2, 2⁻¹, ψ / 2, 0⟩
  inv := star ⟨φ / 2, 2⁻¹, ψ / 2, 0⟩
  val_inv := by rw [self_mul_star, ← coe_one, coe_inj, normSq_def']; grind
  inv_val := by rw [star_mul_self, ← coe_one, coe_inj, normSq_def']; grind

/-- The unit icosians. -/
def Icosian : Subgroup ℍˣ := Subgroup.closure {icosian6, icosian10}

If you make Quaternion instance-reducible, you cannot reliably provide instances for Quaternion that differ from the instances on its unfolded definition. implicit_reducible is the transparency level at which Quaternion cannot looked into when resolving instances, but where it can be unfolded when comparing types or implicit arguments.

Paul Reichert said:
Making it implicit_reducible works too:

But now #43078 makes it an abbrev
Thanks, I didn't see that. Also good, probably even better.
Is the (small) slowdown that I see when I make Quaternion an abbrev to be expected and tolerated, or what?

I think the slowdown could be tolerated but the reason of it is interesting to me, I could surely imagine that with the current abbrev will cause kernel to unfold more but meanwhile it should also fix (some?) defEq issue? Anyways I think the PR is fine with the slowdown but if we could fix the slowdown then it would be a great PR!
According to the latest results the slowdown goes down even more when @[simp high] is used on the lemmas that previously triggered the simpNF linter

Most of the slowdown is in DualQuaternion. It seems that this is because TrivSqZeroExt, the base of DualNumber, is currently defined as a synonym for Prod when it should be a two-field structure. (This may also explain why there is a set_option in DualQuaternion.)
It should nevertheless be preferred to merge #43078 first
#43251 contains a fix to the slowdown
#43307 adds the other lemmas that were present in my initial version of the quaternion-as-abbrev PR
